title: Soliduzz: Finding Miscompilations in Smart-Contract Compilers with Assertion-Driven Equivalence Oracles
authors: Alexander Stromberger, Christoph Hochrainer, Valentin Wüstholz, Maria Christakis
abstract: Smart contracts compiled to the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) can manage high-value assets and are difficult to patch after deployment. Compiler miscompilations are therefore especially dangerous: compilation succeeds, but the generated bytecode does not preserve the semantics of the source program. Existing smart-contract compiler fuzzers either focus on robustness failures or rely on differential oracles that compare compiler configurations. We present Soliduzz, an approach for finding miscompilations in EVM smart-contract compilers using assertion-driven equivalence oracles. Soliduzz uses product programs to encode semantic equivalence as executable assertions. The key shift is to compile these self-checking programs and let off-the-shelf fuzzers and symbolic execution engines explore the resulting bytecode for assertion violations, without requiring compiler-specific support from the analyzer. Soliduzz instantiates this idea with two complementary families of metamorphic transformations. The first starts from equivalent expressions and lifts them into smart-contract code that deliberately exercises EVM-specific features such as storage, data locations, control flow, contract interactions, and inline assembly. The second generalizes Equivalence Modulo Inputs (EMI) from fixed concrete inputs to symbolic input spaces. Our symbolic EMI records coverage in the original computation and uses it to guard mutations in the transformed computation. Together, these transformations produce product programs that assert that paired computations yield the same outputs. We evaluate Soliduzz on three EVM smart-contract compilers (solc, solx, and vyper) using several analysis tools. Overall, Soliduzz exposes 29 bugs. Of these, 24 are compiler bugs: 6 miscompilations, 17 internal compiler errors, and 1 hang. The remaining 5 are bugs in the analysis tools.
title_zh: Soliduzz：使用断言驱动等价性查找智能合约编译器中的错误编译
abstract_zh: 编译为以太坊虚拟机(EVM)的智能合约可以管理高价值资产，并且在部署后难以修补。因此，编译器误编译尤其危险：编译成功，但生成的字节码不保留源程序的语义。现有的智能合约编译器模糊测试工具要么专注于健壮性故障，要么依赖于比较编译器配置的差异预言机。我们提出了Soliduzz，一种使用断言驱动的等价预言机来发现EVM智能合约编译器中误编译的方法。Soliduzz使用产品程序将语义等价编码为可执行的断言。关键的转变在于编译这些自检查程序，并让现成的模糊测试和符号执行引擎探索生成的字节码以查找断言违规，而不需要分析器提供编译器特定的支持。Soliduzz通过两种互补的变形转换家族来实现这一理念。第一种从等价表达式开始，将它们提升为智能合约代码，这些代码刻意使用EVM特定功能，如存储、数据位置、控制流、合约交互和内联汇编。第二种将等价输入模(EMI)从固定的具体输入推广到符号输入空间。我们的符号EMI记录原始计算中的覆盖率，并使用它来保护转换后计算中的变异。这些转换共同生成产品程序，断言配对计算产生相同的输出。我们使用多种分析工具在三个EVM智能合约编译器(solc、solx和vyper)上评估了Soliduzz。总体而言，Soliduzz发现了29个错误，其中24个是编译器错误：6个误编译，17个内部编译器错误，和1个挂起。其余5个是分析工具中的错误。
